members.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
members.content: Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year.

members.title: 同一段 DNA，在不同细胞里命运不同：AlphaGenome 2 把预测拉到细胞级同一套DNA在不同细胞中基因开关迥异，同一突变在不同细胞后果不同，长期阻碍疾病基因定位。11月11日，谷歌DeepMind推出AlphaGenome 2，基于1.07亿单细胞数据，将“基因变异会怎样”精确到单个细胞类型与状态，命中率较上一代几乎翻倍。上一代仅关注组织整体分子活动，难捕捉特定细胞细微差异。 刚刚 6.9K
members.content: 人人带着同一套 DNA，可心肌细胞与抗感染免疫细胞开关的基因天差地别。同一个突变落到不同细胞上结果也可能南辕北辙——正是这层复杂性长期卡住疾病基因定位。当地时间 11 月 11 日，谷歌 DeepMind 推出 AlphaGenome 2，把"基因变异会怎样"的答案精确到单个细胞类型与状态。

members.title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
members.content: Whether you’re planning a family trip, running a rec league or hosting a potluck, coordinating as a group is easier when everyone can pitch in, build and decide together in one place.Today, we’re introducing Tabletop, a new Google Labs experiment built for real-time collaboration.Just add in your links, files, and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets.

members.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
members.content: November 11, 2026 ScienceAdam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga AvsecOur next-generation DNA sequence model bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how genetic variants affect hundreds of human cell types.Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types, giving scientists a powerful new tool to uncover the cellular drivers of disease.Cells are the building blocks of life.

topic_dossiers.topic_title: 数据中心建设面临现实阻碍

members.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
members.content: Loading the player The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to a scramble for electricity. Before those challenges even come into play, though, there’s a more basic problem: A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. With billions of dollars in AI infrastructure investment at stake, separating realistic projects from speculative ones is becoming increasingly important.

members.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
members.content: CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.

members.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
members.content: Frontier AI labs have warned that their technology could help develop dangerous bioweapons.Now, a startup says it has developed a defense. On Wednesday, Radical Numerics announced that it has developed a new edge model called Omnii Defense that is designed to flag natural and AI-engineered pathogens using a laptop and a USB gene sequencer. It can also run without an internet connection, allowing researchers in the field with spotty connections to use it.

members.title: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair
members.content: Congress is gearing up to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to answer their questions about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Bloomberg reports, citing two House Republicans. The report comes a week after House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent a letter to Huang asking him to appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing in regards to his relations with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy.

topic_dossiers.topic_title: 英国 AI 芯片公司 Fractile 融资

members.title: 估值飙升至 70 亿美元！英国 AI 芯片新星 Fractile 获 7.2 亿融资，Anthropic 抢当首批客户总部伦敦的AI芯片初创Fractile（2022年成立）完成7.2亿美元新融资，投后估值达70亿美元，较5月约11亿美元大幅跃升，跻身英国估值最高初创行列。投资方包括多家硅谷知名风投、谷歌旗下独立风投及英国政府主权AI基金，文章还提及其独创半导体技术。 刚刚 7.5K
members.content: 成立于2022年并总部位于伦敦的英国人工智能芯片初创公司 Fractile 近日完成了新一轮7.2亿美元的融资，其投后估值一举达到70亿美元。与今年5月上一轮大约11亿美元的估值相比，其估值迎来了大幅攀升，这也使其迅速跻身英国估值最高的初创公司行列。本轮投资方阵容强大，囊括了多家知名的硅谷风险投资机构、谷歌旗下独立风投部门以及英国政府的主权人工智能基金。独创半导体架构:层叠集成单芯片，瞄准 AI 推理性能瓶颈在技术路线方面，Fractile 主打将定制的内存与计算单元直接层叠集成在单颗芯片之上的全新半导体设计方案。该技术的核心应用场景直指当前的 AI 推理任务，试图从底层解决行业长期面临的计算能力与内存带宽增长严重不匹配的发展瓶颈。根据该公司公布的技术预期，这种创新的半导体设计有望将人工智能的推理响应速度提升足足10倍。正是由于看中了其在硬件性能层面的突破潜力，人工智能头部企业 Anthropic 目前已经表达了强烈的合作意向，有意成为其首批核心客户。资本热潮与量产挑战并存:首款产品计划于明年推出尽管当前全球有大量企业都在积极研发用于对标英伟达的 AI 专用推理芯片，赛道竞争呈现出白热化态势，且近期宏观层面的 AI 行业增长预期也有所降温，但 Fractile 依然凭借其硬核的技术路线赢得了资本市场的青睐。

members.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
members.content: Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated. Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.

members.title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time
members.content: OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources. If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year.

members.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
members.content: Lauren Feiner is a senior policy reporter at The Verge, covering the intersection of Silicon Valley and Capitol Hill. She spent 5 years covering tech policy at CNBC, writing about antitrust, privacy, and content moderation reform.United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns.The company says it hasn’t yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports, in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash.

members.title: I Saw the Future of Robotics in a Virtual Duck That Chases My Cat
members.content: Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI.Using OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol, I taught a virtual version of Microduck—a cute robot from Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face—to walk around a room and identify any bengal cats in its vicinity. (The clip above shows the robot waddling toward a target feline; its eye view is shown top right.)I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck—please hurry up and ship it, guys—but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing.

members.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
members.content: Published on Nov 4 · Submitted by Yu Lei on Nov 11 Authors: , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , Abstract Micius-Flash is a 27B-parameter multimodal reasoning model trained with a knowledge-tree data pipeline and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, achieving strong hardware and semiconductor agent benchmark results and supporting tool-integrated engineering workflows. We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window.

members.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
members.content: View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract:Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge. Each model may require coordinated changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends. Existing coding agents often miss these cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures across host--device execution paths. We present EngineAgent, an agentic system for automating on-device LLM model enablement.
